title: Why Everyone Asks You for a Tip Now (Even Self-Checkout)
alts: Tipping Culture Explained: Why Every Screen Wants 25%
A Machine Asked Me for a 25% Tip. Here's Who Gets It.
line1: Why is everyone asking for a tip now? A self-checkout asked Dave for 25% on a $2.50 water. Here's why, who profits, and when no tip is fine.
summary: Dave scans a $2.50 bottle of water himself and the screen asks for a 20, 25 or 30% tip. We trace tipping in America from the 1800s and the Civil War to the Pullman porters and the state bans of 1909-1926, explain the $2.13 federal tipped minimum wage and the tip credit (Department of Labor), show why payment tablets, preset buttons and the default effect made tip screens explode, and who profits: workers, businesses and card processors taking 2.6% of tips. Then the 2026 data (Toast: 19.3% at sit-down restaurants), the 'no tax on tips' law in plain numbers, and a simple tipping guide.
